title: Welcome, Sweet Day of Rest
description: Welcome, Sweet Day of Rest in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 14, headed “The Lord's day; or, Delight in ordinances”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Wel-come, sweet day of rest, That saw the Lord a-rise; Wel-come to this re-viv-ing breast, And these re-joic-ing eyes!

lines: Here we may sit, and see him here,
And love, and praise, and pray.
Where my dear God hath been,
Is sweeter than ten thousand days
In such a frame as this,
And sit and sing herself away

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
